content.key_idea: Multiple QPUs share one QRAM via a high-bandwidth bus and query queue; panel (b) shows this Fat-Tree design achieves O(log N) query latency and parallelism versus O(log^2 N) for Bucket-Brigade QRAM at the same O(N) qubit cost.
content.reading_order: Panel (a) on the left shows the QPU array feeding down through the bus and query queue into the shared QRAM; panel (b) on the right is a table comparing Fat-Tree against Bucket-Brigade QRAM costs.

summary: Fat-Tree QRAM is a shared quantum random access memory architecture that lets multiple QPUs pipeline independent queries in parallel, unlike the Bucket-Brigade (BB) QRAM baseline where a single query occupies the whole tree. Panel (a) is a schematic showing three QPUs in a QPU Array connected via a Quantum High-bandwidth Bus down to a Query Queue, which double-arrows into the Shared QRAM box, illustrating that many QPUs contend for one memory resource. Panel (b) is a small comparison table contrasting Fat-Tree QRAM (this work) against Shared BB QRAM across four metrics in Big-O notation: qubit count (both O(N)), query parallelism (log(N) vs 1), query latency (log(N) vs log^2(N)), and fidelity, showing Fat-Tree's asymptotic advantage in enabling parallel queries without sacrificing qubit-count scaling.
summary_zh: 面板(a)展示多个 QPU 通过高带宽总线和查询队列共享同一 QRAM 的架构；面板(b)用大 O 表格对比 Fat-Tree QRAM 与 Bucket-Brigade QRAM 在比特数、并行度、延迟和保真度上的差异，凸显本文方案的并行优势。
